what: Core Web Vitals are three user-focused metrics: LCP (how fast the main content appears), INP (how quickly the page responds to clicks and keys) and CLS (how much the layout jumps). A page passes when the 75th percentile of real visits is in the 'good' range for all three.
like: Like a restaurant review with three questions: did the food arrive quickly, did the waiter respond when I called, and did the table wobble while I ate?
why: They turn 'feels fast' into numbers the whole team can track
They are measured on real users, so they reflect real phones and networks
Each one points to a specific kind of fix (loading, responsiveness, stability)

nodes.t: Field data|CrUX or your RUM, p75
Fix by cause|LCP parts, long tasks, reserved space

steps.d: LCP is when the largest image or text block is shown. INP is the worst click, tap or key latency of the visit. CLS is the largest burst of unexpected layout movement.
Good at the 75th percentile: LCP 2.5 s or less, INP 200 ms or less, CLS 0.1 or less. Poor is above 4 s, 500 ms and 0.25. Measure mobile and desktop separately.
CrUX (via PageSpeed Insights) or your own RUM shows what real users get. Use it to decide what to fix first.
Lighthouse and DevTools give repeatable traces for debugging. They can't predict INP, which depends on real interactions.
LCP splits into TTFB, resource load delay, load duration and render delay. INP splits into input delay, processing and presentation. CLS comes from unsized media, late content, fonts and ads.
Put budgets and Lighthouse CI in the pipeline and re-check field data after each release.

numbers.l: Good LCP at the 75th percentile (needs improvement up to 4 s, poor above)
Good INP at the 75th percentile (poor above 500 ms); INP replaced FID
Good CLS at the 75th percentile (poor above 0.25)
Ideal share of LCP for TTFB, resource load delay, load duration, element render delay

tool: PageSpeed Insights, Lighthouse, Chrome DevTools, web-vitals

choices.d: Field data (CrUX, RUM) shows reality and sets priorities. Lab data (Lighthouse) is repeatable for debugging and CI. Use both; trust field when they disagree.
Find the weakest of the three at p75 and the biggest LCP subpart. Optimising one subpart can just move time to another, so re-measure.
Quantity budgets (JS KB, image MB) and metric budgets (LCP, TBT) in CI catch regressions early. Lighthouse weights TBT 30%, LCP 25% and CLS 25% in its score.
SSR or static HTML puts content in the first response (helps LCP); less client JavaScript helps INP; reserved space fixes CLS.

instead.why: How to measure these metrics on real users
A tool for lowering TTFB and getting content on screen sooner

breaks.t: Great Lighthouse score, poor field LCP
breaks.d: Lab used a fast device and a different LCP element than real users see.
breaks.see: CrUX LCP is orange or red while Lighthouse is green
breaks.fix: Trust field data, segment by device and network, check the actual LCP element in RUM

breaks.t: INP regresses after adding a library
breaks.d: A third-party script or a heavy handler blocks the main thread.
breaks.see: Long tasks over 50 ms around clicks
breaks.fix: Break up work with scheduler.yield, defer or remove the script, shrink DOM

breaks.d: Banners, ads, fonts or images arrive without reserved space.
breaks.see: Content jumps as the page loads
breaks.fix: Set width and height or aspect-ratio, reserve slots, use font-display and matching fallback metrics

say: The three Core Web Vitals are LCP at 2.5 seconds, INP at 200 milliseconds and CLS at 0.1, judged at the 75th percentile of real users, split by device.
I start from field data to find what to fix, use Lighthouse and DevTools traces to reproduce it, and keep budgets in CI so it doesn't regress.
For LCP I look at the four subparts, for INP at long tasks and DOM size, and for CLS at anything that loads without reserved space.

followups.a: It shows the experience of most users without being dominated by outliers, and it is what Google uses to judge pass or fail. Averages hide the slow tail.
FID only measured the delay before the first interaction. INP covers all interactions across the visit and includes processing and presentation time.

today: The Core Web Vitals set is LCP, INP and CLS (INP replaced FID). Field data from CrUX is the reference, Lighthouse scores TBT as a lab proxy for responsiveness, and the web-vitals library with attribution makes it practical to find which element or interaction caused a poor score.

check.q: Which metric replaced First Input Delay?
check.why: INP measures all interactions, not just the first.

check.q: Where must a page score 'good' to pass?
check.a: At the 75th percentile of real page loads for all three metrics
check.why: Pass/fail is based on p75 of field data, split by mobile and desktop.

check.a: Images, ads or fonts that load without reserved space
check.why: Late content pushes existing content around; reserve the space up front.
